Electrical Appliance Sectional Committee, ETD 32

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of lndian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Electrical Appliances Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. The standard covers the general and safety requirements safety against electric shock, safety against the effect of performance requirements and the list of performance evaluation of these characteristics for coffee makers will for electric coffee makers to ensure personal excessive temperature and fire, etc. The characteristics along with the method for be covered in a separate Indian Standard.

For the sake of convenience of reference the format of the standard has been followed with the pattern followed in IS 302-I ( 1979 ) `Safety of household and similar electrical appliances : Part 1 General requirements (Jifth revision )`. with IS 302-l ( 1979 ). For the sake of This standard is to be read in conjunction convenience, the clauses of this standard correspond to those of IS 302-I ( 1979 ) which are applicable ( which means that relevant provisions of the clause shall apply ), or not applicable and the sub-clauses or portions thereof which are not applicable are indicated as under: a) In case of a clause where it is applicable or not applicable, the wording used is `This clause of IS 302-I ( 1979 ) is applicable/not applicable'. b) In case of a sub-clause or part thereof the wording used is `Not applicable'. Wherever a sub-clause of 302-I ( 1979 ) is to be replaced by a new test, it has been indicated under: Replacement followed by the new text. indicated as as

Any addition to the existing provisions of a sub-clause of IS 302-l ( 1979 ) has been under: Addition followed by the text of the additional matter.

Clauses/tables which are additional to those of IS 302-l ( 1979 ) are numbered starting from 101 and additional sub-clauses are numbered with the main clauses number followed by 101, 102 etc, for example, 7.101. Should however any deviations exist between IS 302-I ( 1979 ) and this standard, of latter shall apply. the provisions

The Indian Standards which are necessary adjuncts to this standard are given in Annex AA. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

22.101 The body of the coffee percolator shall be made of copper, brass, stainless steel, aluminium or any other suitable material. Aluminium used in the construction of coffee percolator shall conform to tither IS 20 : 1977 or IS 21 : 1975. In case of brass or copper the interior surface of the coffee percolator, spout and lid shall be protected by a coating of minimum thickness of .025 mm of pure tin, nickle or other suitable material that shall give equal protection and shall not cause contamination of the water. In case of other metals also similar protective coating, wherever necessary, shall bc provided. 22.102 Handles, grips, knobs and such other parts that may have to be touched during the working of the appliance shall be of electrically non-conducting and heat-insulating material. Handles and grips shall be so fixed that they do not rotate even in the event of slackening of the means of fixing. 22.103 The immersion heating element shall be so designed and located as not to interfere with the easy cleaning of the coffee percolator. 22.104 The spout or tap shall be so constructed to give a cleanpouring action. as

22.109 The cover or lid, if of transparent material, shall be capable of withstanding the heating to which it is subjected during its normal use. There shall be no damage to the cover or lid during the mechanical strength test, test for abnormal operation, and the endurance test. 22.110 The coffee makers shall be incorporated

IS 302-2-206 : 1994 101 TESTS 101.1 Type Tests The tests specified in Table 101 shall constitute the type tests and shall be carried out on two samples of coffee percolators of the same type and rating selected preferably at random from a regular production lot. Before commencement of the tests, the coffee percolators shall be visually examined and inspected for obvious visual defects in respect of components, parts and their assembly, construction, mechanical hazards, markings, provision of suitable terminals for supply connections, earthing and the effectiveness of screws and connections. The external surface finish shall be even and free from finishing defects. 101.1.1 Criteria of Acceptance 101.3 Routing Test shall constitute Test a) Protection against shock b) High voltage c) Earthing connection of Type Tests electric the routine tests:

Both samples shall successfully pass all the type tests for proving conformity with the requirements of the standard. If any of the samples fails in any of the type tests, the testing authority at its discretion, may call for fresh samples not exceeding twice the original number and subject them again to all tests or to the test(s) in which failure(s) had occurred.
